import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes and p-values for each feature
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        x = feats.x[:, i]
        y = feats.y
        mean_diff = np.mean(x[y==1]) - np.mean(x[y==0])
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x[y==1], x[y==0], equal_var=False)
        effects.append((fid, abs(mean_diff), abs(t_stat), p_val))
    
    # Sort by effect size (mean difference)
    effects.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Select top candidates, removing near-duplicates
    selected = []
    seen = set()
    for fid, _, _, _ in effects:
        if fid in seen:
            continue
        # Check correlation with already selected features
        is_duplicate = False
        for sel_fid in selected:
            col_a = feats.column(sel_fid)
            col_b = feats.column(fid)
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col_a], feats.x[:, col_b])[0,1]) > 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        if not is_duplicate:
            selected.append(fid)
            seen.add(fid)
            if len(selected) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                break
    
    # If no strong signals, return empty design
    if not selected:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # For the mechanism, use the strongest feature(s) 
    drivers = tuple(selected[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # Include only the selected features for modeling to keep it small
    columns = tuple(selected)
    
    # No interactions to keep model small
    products = ()
    
    # Simple weighted score based on effect sizes
    loadings = {}
    for fid in selected:
        effect = next((e[2] for e in effects if e[0] == fid), 0)
        loadings[fid] = effect
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
